review.summary: PR #12 fixes issue #8, where JuliaSyntax's Core parsing hooks caused `Meta.parse` on invalid syntax to raise a `MethodError: Cannot convert ... JuliaSyntax.ParseError to ... String` instead of the expected `Base.Meta.ParseError`. The change touches src/hooks.jl and src/parser.jl (4 hunks) and adds test/hooks.jl (registered in runtests.jl), with the trigger test 'Hooks for Core integration'. This is a production behavior fix to an existing, already-shipped integration path, not a new API.
review.validation_risks: The PR bundles two behavioral changes ('ParseError works with Meta.parse' and 'incremental parsing of statements works'); the second could be closer to completing partially-implemented hook behavior, which would weaken the single-defect framing and may require splitting or restricting the trigger test to the ParseError case. The trigger test list is very noisy (hundreds of 'Parse <file>.jl' cases over Base and JuliaSyntax sources), suggesting the harness selected the whole suite; those cases are slow, environment/Julia-version dependent, and likely unrelated to the defect. Tests exercising Core hooks via enable_in_core! mutate global parser state and can be order-dependent or non-reentrant, a flakiness risk. Repository is early-stage, so surrounding APIs may have shifted.

swe.problem_statement:
Meta.parse on invalid syntax with enable_in_core!
I noticed that the errors are different:

```julia-repl
julia> Meta.parse("[(1,2]")
ERROR: Base.Meta.ParseError("unexpected \"]\" in argument list")
Stacktrace:
 [1] #parse#3
   @ ./meta.jl:237 [inlined]
 [2] parse(str::String; raise::Bool, depwarn::Bool)
   @ Base.Meta ./meta.jl:268
 [3] parse(str::String)
   @ Base.Meta ./meta.jl:268
 [4] top-level scope
   @ REPL[1]:1

julia> using JuliaSyntax

julia> JuliaSyntax.enable_in_core!()

julia> Meta.parse("[(1,2]")
ERROR: MethodError: Cannot `convert` an object of type JuliaSyntax.ParseError to an object of type String
Closest candidates are:
  convert(::Type{String}, ::String) at /Applications/Julia-1.7 x86.app/Contents/Resources/julia/share/julia/base/essentials.jl:223
  convert(::Type{T}, ::T) where T<:AbstractString at /Applications/Julia-1.7 x86.app/Contents/Resources/julia/share/julia/base/strings/basic.jl:231
  convert(::Type{T}, ::AbstractString) where T<:AbstractString at /Applications/Julia-1.7 x86.app/Contents/Resources/julia/share/julia/base/strings/basic.jl:232
  ...
Stacktrace:
 [1] Base.Meta.ParseError(msg::JuliaSyntax.ParseError)
   @ Base.Meta ./meta.jl:190
 [2] #parse#3
   @ ./meta.jl:237 [inlined]
 [3] parse(str::String; raise::Bool, depwarn::Bool)
   @ Base.Meta ./meta.jl:268
 [4] parse(str::String)
   @ Base.Meta ./meta.jl:268
 [5] top-level scope
   @ none:1
```

Not sure if this matters or not, just thought i would report it

swe.interface:
Function: enable_in_core!()
Location: JuliaSyntax module
Inputs: none
Outputs: nothing (sets an internal flag that makes the Julia runtime use JuliaSyntax's `core_parser_hook` for parsing)
Description: Enables integration of JuliaSyntax with the Julia Core parser so that subsequent calls to `Meta.parse` delegate to the JuliaSyntax parser.

Function: disable_in_core!()
Location: JuliaSyntax module
Inputs: none
Outputs: nothing (clears the flag set by `enable_in_core!`)
Description: Disables the JuliaSyntax‑Core integration, restoring the default flisp‑based parser for `Meta.parse`.

Function: core_parser_hook(code::String, filename::String, lineno::LineNumberNode, offset::Int, options)
Location: src/hooks.jl (called by Core._parse when Core integration is enabled)
Inputs:
  - `code`: source code string to be parsed.
  - `filename`: name of the source file (used for diagnostics).
  - `lineno`: a `LineNumberNode` indicating the starting line number for the code.
  - `offset`: byte offset in the original source where parsing should begin (0‑based for Core).
  - `options`: parsing mode; either `:all` for a full file or a specific rule symbol.
Outputs:
  - Returns a `Core.svec` containing the parsed expression (or `Expr(:error, ...)`) and the last byte offset after parsing.
  - Throws `JuliaSyntax.ParseError` on syntax errors (wrapped in an `Expr(:error)` which Meta.parse propagates as a `JuliaSyntax.ParseError`).
Description: Core hook that drives the JuliaSyntax parser when the runtime asks for parsing; the added `lineno` argument aligns the signature with the newer Julia Core API.

Function: core_parser_hook(code::String, filename::String, offset::Int, options)
Location: src/hooks.jl (compatibility overload)
Inputs:
  - `code`, `filename`, `offset`, `options` as above.
Outputs:
  - Delegates to the five‑argument `core_parser_hook` with a dummy line number `LineNumberNode(0)`.
Description: Backward‑compatible wrapper preserving the old four‑argument signature; kept so existing calls from older Julia versions continue to work.

llm_metadata.reasoning: The issue reports that after calling JuliaSyntax.enable_in_core!(), Meta.parse throws a MethodError instead of a JuliaSyntax.ParseError, and expects the parser to return the JuliaSyntax error type. The provided test patch adds a hooks test that enables core integration, checks normal parsing results, and verifies that Meta.parse throws JuliaSyntax.ParseError on invalid syntax, directly matching the reported behavior. No external dependencies, naming expectations, or ambiguous specifications are present, so the task is cleanly specified and test-aligned.
